newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-SPARTAK BLAST "FASCIST" POLICE FOR BEATING FANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPARTAK BLAST "FASCIST" POLICE FOR BEATING FANS.

text.p: Baton-wielding riot police beat dozens of teenage Spartak Moscow fans during a Russian Cup game at second-division Noginsk this week, Spartak club officials said on Thursday.
The officials condemned the police action during Tuesday's game as "fascist barbarism".

"It's a miracle no one was killed," Spartak chairman and head coach Oleg Romantsev and team captain Ilya Tsymbalar wrote in an open letter to fans in Thursday's Moskovsky Komsomolets newspaper. Spartak won the match 1-0.
Romantsev, former coach of the Russian national side, intended to complain to Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov, Spartak vice-president Gregory Yesaulenko said.
Under the headline "Spartak Don't Play for the Commandos", the club said police grossly overreacted to the throwing of a smoke bomb by a fan in the 75th minute of the match.
"What happened in Noginsk was barbarity...There was a lot of blood," Yesaulenko said. "The local OMON (police commandos) beat everyone at random. These aren't people but fascists."
The deputy police chief of Noginsk, 70 km (45 miles) southeast of Moscow, denied the charge on Thursday. He said there was no serious incident and no injuries.
Sport-Express newspaper published an eyewitness account and a photograph of a police commando clubbing a supporter.
Yesaulenko said the injured, mainly boys aged between 14 and 17, were too afraid to seek medical help in Noginsk and were mostly taken home to the capital by friends.
Police commanders refused an appeal by club coaches to call off their men.

In a separate incident on Tuesday night, hardcore supporters of army team CSKA Moscow battled opposing fans and OMON police in the Moscow suburb of Ramenskoye after CKSA beat first-division Saturn 2-0 in the Cup. RIA news agency quoted police saying several fans were injured, one seriously.
Last October, more than 50 people were hurt when hundreds of angry CSKA fans went on the rampage after losing a league match.
